report_name: 'BigBear 2.0' Phishing Service Bypasses MFA in Global M365 Campaign

threat_actors.name: General Boss
threat_actors.description: The alleged operator of the 'BigBear 2.0' Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platform, managing the infrastructure and leasing access to affiliates.

threat_actors.name: BigBear 2.0 Affiliates
threat_actors.description: At least five affiliate operators who lease access to the BigBear 2.0 PhaaS platform to conduct phishing campaigns against organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The attack is initiated when a victim clicks a link in a phishing email, directing them to a malicious server that proxies the legitimate Microsoft login page.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: The BigBear 2.0 framework performs an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attack by proxying the legitimate Microsoft login page to intercept credentials and session cookies between the victim and Microsoft.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The primary goal of the AiTM attack is to intercept and steal the session cookie generated after a successful MFA-authenticated login, allowing the attacker to bypass MFA and take over the session.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Stolen credentials and session cookies are used to gain unauthorized access to legitimate Microsoft 365 user accounts.

attack_patterns.name: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: The AiTM phishing attack and subsequent session hijacking all occur over standard web protocols (HTTPS) to blend in with normal traffic and for command and control.

attack_patterns.name: Impair Defenses
attack_patterns.description: The framework uses custom JavaScript injections to attempt to disable or downgrade modern, phishing-resistant MFA methods like FIDO2/WebAuthn.

attack_patterns.name: Proxy
attack_patterns.description: The operation uses geo-matched residential proxy pools to make login attempts with stolen credentials appear legitimate and bypass bot detection and location-based Conditional Access policies.

malware.name: BigBear 2.0
malware.description: A Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) toolkit, based on a customized version of Evilginx2, designed for adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks to bypass MFA on Microsoft 365 accounts.

tools.name: Evilginx2
tools.description: The core framework used and customized for the 'BigBear 2.0' PhaaS. It is used to perform the adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attack to proxy the login page and steal credentials and session cookies.

tools.name: Telegram
tools.description: Used by the BigBear 2.0 service to deliver stolen credentials and session cookies to affiliate operators in real-time via bots.

campaigns.name: BigBear 2.0 Campaign
campaigns.description: A large-scale Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) operation active since at least June 2026, targeting Microsoft 365 users globally to steal credentials and session cookies using AiTM techniques.
campaigns.objective: Steal Microsoft 365 credentials and session cookies to enable account takeover and potential supply chain attacks.

identities.name: IT Service Providers
identities.description: A primary target category for the BigBear 2.0 campaign, likely to enable downstream supply chain attacks.

identities.name: Managed Service Providers (MSPs)
identities.description: A primary target category for the BigBear 2.0 campaign, likely to enable downstream supply chain attacks.

infrastructure.name: BigBear 2.0 AiTM Proxy Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A network of 42 VPS nodes, primarily hosted at Vultr, used to proxy legitimate Microsoft login pages for adversary-in-the-middle attacks.

infrastructure.name: Residential Proxy Pools
infrastructure.description: Geo-matched residential proxies used to make login attempts with stolen credentials appear legitimate and bypass location-based Conditional Access policies.

indicators.name: Anomalous M365 Session Token Replay
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous M365 Session Token Replay
id: 9c8b7a6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: 'Detects a Microsoft 365 sign-in where MFA was satisfied by a claim in the token, which can indicate a replayed session cookie from an Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing attack. Further correlation with anomalous IP, location, or device information is recommended.'
references:
  - https://www.cloudsek.com/blog/tracking-bigbear-2-0-evilginx2-phishing-campaign
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-08
tags:
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    MfaDetail: 'MFA requirement satisfied by claim in the token'
    ResultType: 0
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Microsoft Entra ID sign-ins where MFA was satisfied by a claim in the token. This can be a sign of a replayed session cookie stolen via an AiTM attack, as seen in the BigBear 2.0 campaign. Analysts should investigate for anomalous IP addresses, locations, or device information associated with the login.
